name: Tennessee

law.summary: Permittees must report any release that could threaten health or the environment to TDEC within 24 hours and in writing within five days; SSOs are prohibited outright. No duty to tell the public was found; TDEC itself publishes the reports in its Events Report table.

citations.title: Twenty-four hour reporting
citations.quote: In the case of any noncompliance, or any release (whether or not caused by improper operation and maintenance), which could cause a threat to human health or the environment, the permittee shall: 1. Report the noncompliance or release to the Commissioner within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances.
citations.deadline: 24 hours; written report within five days
citations.threshold: any release which could cause a threat to human health or the environment

citations.title: SSO prohibition
citations.quote: For publicly owned treatment works (POTW) or domestic wastewater treatment plants, sanitary sewer overflows, including dry-weather overflows and wet weather overflows, are prohibited.

bills_and_cases: Nashville Metro consent decree (2009, Clean Water Nashville); Tennessee Riverkeeper suit over Nashville overflows (2019-2020, search only).
No 2025-2026 bill on public notice found (search only).

erule.notes: MyTDEC Forms; TDEC's own Events Report is the public output. Not in EPA SOBE.

statewide_feed.coordinates: none in the table; the Events Map page has points (APEX AJAX, untested)
statewide_feed.start_end: start date; end date and duration (end often blank)
statewide_feed.license: no licence; disclaimer 'informational purposes only and should not be used to determine compliance'
statewide_feed.notes: No CSO events (permitted discharges); Memphis absent.

cso.notification_practice: No CSO event notice found for Nashville, Chattanooga or Clarksville; CSOs are permitted and not in the TDEC table.

sso.location_source: TDEC Events Report addresses (geocodable); Events Map points
sso.notes: Addresses are street addresses of the overflow, sometimes with trailing spaces.

beaches.program: No state beach monitoring program found; TDEC water-contact advisories; TVA and Corps manage reservoir beaches
beaches.notes: Corps beaches (Cordell Hull, Center Hill) closed by press release.

habs.program: TDEC HAB response program (dashboard, Survey123 layer, story map)
habs.notes: Public layer exposes reporters' contact details; use advisory fields only.

outfalls.cso_inventory_gap: unknown (3 permits, 17 outfalls in EPA inventory)

barriers.what: No public notice duty; operators do not post CSO events
tn.gov pages return 403 to curl (WebFetch works); the APEX viewer needs a session cookie
Events Report disclaimer: informational only, not for compliance
barriers.note: Quote it; it does not forbid reuse.

readiness.rationale: One public CSV of every SSO, release and bypass since 2020, refreshed with about a five-day lag. Day precision, no receiving water (trace from geocoded address), no CSO events, Memphis missing.

owner_questions: Day-precision events: show them as dated events (yellow 72 hours from the start date) or mark them like the monthly reports?
Geocode the event address to place SSOs (no coordinates in the CSV) or scrape the Events Map points?
Raise with TDEC that its public HAB layer exposes reporters' phone numbers and emails?
Memphis has no rows: ask TDEC or the city?
surprise: Tennessee publishes all 12,857 sewer overflow and release reports since 2020 as a one-click CSV, yet the state's biggest city, Memphis, has no rows, and CSOs (Nashville, Chattanooga) never appear because they are permitted discharges.
